message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
My best reading is **sinus rhythm at about 67 beats/minute, with a pattern suggesting right bundle branch block (RBBB)**—a delay in electrical conduction through the right side of the heart.

- **Rhythm:** Regular, with a P wave before each heartbeat.
- **Axis:** Appears normal.
- **Conduction:** The QRS complexes appear widened, with a prominent terminal R wave in V1 and terminal S waves in I/V6, supporting RBBB.
- **ST/T waves:** Inversion in V1 can accompany RBBB. I don’t see an obvious acute ST-elevation heart attack pattern, but this image cannot exclude a heart attack.

RBBB can be an incidental finding; whether it needs investigation depends on symptoms, medical history, and whether it is new. A clinician should confirm the measurements and compare with an earlier ECG. [RBBB reference](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK507872/)

**If you currently have chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or severe dizziness, seek emergency care.**

How old is the person, why was the ECG taken, and are there any symptoms?
